title: Ch 1 Test (Set B): Chemical Reactions and Equations
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
Write balanced chemical equations wherever asked.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a chemical change?
questions.answer: (d) Melting of ice (only the state changes; no new substance is formed)

questions.q: In the reaction 2H_{2}S + SO_{2} → 3S + 2H_{2}O, the substance that is oxidised is:
Which of these is an endothermic process?
questions.answer: (b) Decomposition of calcium carbonate (it needs heat)

questions.q: When lead nitrate is heated strongly, the products are:
options: lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen
questions.answer: (a) lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. 2Pb(NO_{3})_{2} → 2PbO + 4NO_{2} + O_{2}

questions.q: A balanced chemical equation has equal numbers of:
options: atoms of each element on both sides
questions.answer: (b) atoms of each element on both sides

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** Packets of chips are flushed with nitrogen gas.
**Reason (R):** Nitrogen is a highly reactive gas that kills bacteria.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (c). Nitrogen is used because it is unreactive. It replaces oxygen and prevents rancidity.

questions.q: What is an oxidation reaction? Identify the substance oxidised in: 4Na + O_{2} → 2Na_{2}O.
questions.answer: A reaction in which a substance gains oxygen (or loses hydrogen). In 4Na + O_{2} → 2Na_{2}O, sodium is oxidised, because it gains oxygen.

or.q: Write one balanced equation each for a decomposition reaction in which the energy is supplied as (a) heat and (b) light.
or.answer: (a) CaCO_{3} → CaO + CO_{2} (on heating). (b) 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br_{2} (in sunlight).

questions.q: Why do we paint iron articles? Name the process that this prevents.
questions.answer: Paint forms a layer that stops air (oxygen) and moisture from reaching the iron. This prevents rusting, which is a type of corrosion.

questions.q: A shiny brown element X becomes black when heated in air.

subparts.q: Identify X and the black substance.
subparts.answer: X is copper (Cu). The black substance is copper(II) oxide (CuO).
Combination reaction (also an oxidation of copper).

questions.q: Explain each of the following with one balanced equation: (i) displacement reaction, (ii) double displacement reaction, (iii) redox reaction.
questions.answer: (i) A more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound: Fe + CuSO_{4} → FeSO_{4} + Cu. (ii) Two compounds exchange ions: Na_{2}SO_{4} + BaCl_{2} → BaSO_{4} + 2NaCl. (iii) One substance is oxidised while another is reduced: ZnO + C → Zn + CO (C is oxidised, ZnO is reduced).

or.q: Write balanced equations for what happens when: (a) zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid, (b) quicklime reacts with water, (c) electric current is passed through water.

subparts.q: What is corrosion? What is rust, and what conditions does iron need to rust? Give two ways to prevent rusting.
subparts.answer: Corrosion is the slow eating away of a metal when it reacts with substances around it, such as air, moisture and acids. Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe_{2}O_{3}·xH_{2}O). Iron rusts only when both air (oxygen) and water are present. Prevention (any two): painting, oiling or greasing, galvanising, making alloys.

subparts.q: What is rancidity? Give two ways to prevent it.
subparts.answer: Fats and oils in food get oxidised, so the food's smell and taste change. Prevention (any two): add antioxidants; store in airtight containers; flush packets with nitrogen; keep in a refrigerator.

or.q:
(a) Balance these equations: (i) Fe_{2}O_{3} + Al → Al_{2}O_{3} + Fe  (ii) BaCl_{2} + K_{2}SO_{4} → BaSO_{4} + KCl  (iii) Ca(OH)_{2} + CO_{2} → CaCO_{3} + H_{2}O [3]
(b) Why is it necessary to balance a chemical equation? [2]
or.answer: (a) (i) Fe_{2}O_{3} + 2Al → Al_{2}O_{3} + 2Fe  (ii) BaCl_{2} + K_{2}SO_{4} → BaSO_{4} + 2KCl  (iii) Ca(OH)_{2} + CO_{2} → CaCO_{3} + H_{2}O (already balanced). (b) Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction (law of conservation of mass), so the number of atoms of each element must be the same on both sides.
marking: (b) law of conservation of mass 1, equal atoms 1

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: A student filled a plastic mug with water and added a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid. Two carbon electrodes were fixed in the mug and connected to a 6 V battery. Test tubes filled with water were inverted over the electrodes. After some time, gas collected in both test tubes, and the volume of gas in one tube was double that in the other.

subparts.q: Why were a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid added to the water?
subparts.answer: Pure water is a very poor conductor of electricity. The acid provides ions so that current can flow.

subparts.q: Which gas was collected in the larger volume?
Write the balanced equation and name the type of reaction. How would you test the gas collected in the smaller volume?
subparts.answer: 2H_{2}O → 2H_{2} + O_{2}. This is a decomposition (electrolytic) reaction. The smaller volume is oxygen, which relights a glowing splinter.
